newsitem.title: PERU: Peru govt halts Iscaycruz zinc output - official.
newsitem.headline: Peru govt halts Iscaycruz zinc output - official.

text.p: Energy and Mines Ministry forced Peru's largest zinc miner, Iscaycruz S.A., to suspend production for environmental reasons, a ministry source said Thursday.
"We are doing everything we can to present the right documentation to get the suspension lifted," said a company source who asked not to be named.
The sources would not say when the company had stopped production but industry sources said the ministry's stoppage order was issued in the last few days.
Another company source said only part of Iscaycruz's production had been affected by the suspension.
He said the suspension was due to the company's "failure to comply with administrative formalities" asking the ministry for permits to move tailings.
In July Iscaycruz, which is controlled by Switzerland's Glencore Group, started production of zinc concentrates and expected to be operating fully at a rate of 125,000 tonnes a year this month.
The company source said he expected operations to be back to normal next week.
The suspension "will in no way affect production in the medium- and long-term," he added.

The Iscaycruz mine -- situated more than 4,500 meters (15,000 feet) above sea level in the Andean province of Oyon 100 miles (160 km) northeast of Lima -- also has a capacity to produce around 9,000 tonnes annually of lead concentrates.

Iscaycruz expects to exploit for at least seven years its proven and probable mineral reserves of 2.7 million tonnes, which have one of the highest zinc grades in the world at 21.4 percent. The reserves' lead grade is 2.2 percent.
